name: showreel-c3-greek-colour

voice.text: These white statues were once painted. So why do we picture marble statues pure white? Over two thousand years, sun, rain and burial wore most of the paint away. But tiny traces survive, and ultraviolet light makes them show. Turns out, one ancient blue still glows in infrared, so cameras can map it.

caption:
Did you picture Greek statues pure white? 🎨

They were once painted. Ancient Greek marble sculptures were painted in bright colours. Over two thousand years, sun, rain and burial wore most of the paint away, but tiny traces survive, and ultraviolet light helps researchers see them. The best part: Egyptian blue, one of the oldest man-made pigments, still glows in infrared when light hits it, so a special camera can map exactly where the blue was painted.

White or painted: what did you picture? Comment one word, and send this to the friend who loves museums.
